name: Crunchbase Startup Ecosystem API — funding rounds, acquisitions, investments (daily event-arrival counts per region/sector)
license: Crunchbase commercial API license (free Basic tier exists but is rate-limited; time-series extraction likely needs Enterprise/Data license)
estimated_length: 12+ years (founding of Crunchbase; ~2010 onwards), with live daily events continuing post-cutoff
contamination_reasoning: Crunchbase API requires a commercial license key for meaningful data access. The event-arrival time series (daily counts of funding announcements by sector/region) is not a standard TSFM benchmark dataset and is unlikely to appear in any pretraining corpus in time-series form. The underlying events are public knowledge but the aggregated count series is a derived product unlikely to be pre-packaged.
gap_filled: econ_fin/irregular — startup funding/acquisition event-arrival series (boom/bust regime shifts, not trivially periodic)
difficulty_note: Funding event counts exhibit strong regime-switching behavior (VC boom cycles, COVID dips, economic downturns) with multi-modal seasonality. Seasonal-naive would fail badly during funding winters or AI-investment spikes. Separates models that handle breaks/regime shifts from those that don't.
adapter_notes: Auth via X-Title-Page and user_key header (Basic) or Bearer token (Enterprise). Rate-limited on Basic tier. Events endpoint returns JSON; aggregate by date=announcement_date, filter by funding_type, location, category. Paginate via offset/limit.
verify: Confirm the free Basic tier still permits enough daily requests to build and maintain a ~200-series panel. Check whether the /funding-rounds and /acquisitions endpoints return the fields needed (announced_on date, country, industry) without Enterprise license.

name: Hybrid Analysis (CrowdStrike) Public API — new malware analysis report submission stream (hourly/daily arrival counts)
license: Hybrid Analysis Community API (free, API key required; rate-limited)
estimated_series_count: ~30–50 (submission count per malware family / file type / verdict, hourly or daily aggregates)
estimated_length: 7+ years (platform active since ~2016), live submissions ongoing
contamination_reasoning: Hybrid Analysis is a malware analysis sandbox platform. The submission stream requires API key authentication and is not a standard TSFM benchmark dataset. The hourly/daily count of analysis submissions (by verdict, file type, or malware family) is unlikely to appear in any pretraining corpus as a time series. Different host from all ALREADY_PROPOSED malware feeds (Shodan, AbuseIPDB, MalwareBazaar, ThreatFox, URLhaus).
gap_filled: web_cloudops/irregular — malware analysis submission event-arrival stream (cybersecurity regime changes, campaign bursts)
difficulty_note: Submission counts have no regular seasonal pattern — they spike on vulnerability disclosures (Patch Tuesday), campaign launches, and 0-day events, with regime shifts during major threat landscape changes. Trivially periodic baselines would miss these entirely.
adapter_notes: Auth via api-key header (free Community API key). GET /api/v2/submissions?limit=100&from=YYYY-MM-DD for recent submissions. Aggregate by created_at timestamp. Rate-limited to ~2000 requests/min on Community tier.
verify: Confirm the /api/v2/submissions endpoint exists and returns created_at timestamps. Check whether the Community (free) tier permits enough lookback or whether historical bulk download is needed. Confirm the host www.hybrid-analysis.com is not already wired or key-gated under a different name.

name: Tomorrow.io (formerly ClimaCell) Weather API — severe weather alert issuance stream and real-time station observations
license: Tomorrow.io commercial API (free Developer tier: 500 calls/day; time-series panel may need paid plan)
estimated_series_count: ~20–50 (alert count per region × alert-type, daily or sub-hourly aggregates)
estimated_length: 4+ years (commercial platform since ~2020; historical archive via paid plan)
contamination_reasoning: Tomorrow.io is a commercial weather API requiring an API key. Its alert-issuance time series (daily count of severe weather alerts by region/type) is a derived product not found in any known TSFM benchmark or pretraining corpus. The underlying weather data may be similar to NWS/NOAA but the alert product, API, and aggregation pipeline are proprietary. Different host from all NWS/NOAA/NCAR sources in either list.
gap_filled: nature/irregular — severe weather alert issuance event-arrival stream (climate-change-driven regime shifts, hurricane seasonality)
difficulty_note: Alert issuance has seasonal structure (storm seasons) but also regime shifts (climate change increases alert frequency; polar vortex events). Non-trivial because alert counts during hurricane season vs. off-season have very different distributions, and year-over-year trends are non-stationary.
adapter_notes: Auth via apikey query parameter or Authorization header. GET /v4/timelines for historical/forecast. GET /v4/alerts for active alerts. Free tier: 500 calls/day. Paginate via startTime/endTime. Historical data may require paid plan.
verify: Confirm the /v4/alerts endpoint returns historical alerts (not just current). Check whether the free Developer tier provides sufficient historical lookback for 320+ observation windows. Confirm host api.tomorrow.io is not already wired or key-gated under a prior Climacell name.

name: ReliefWeb (UN OCHA) API — disaster event alert/report arrival stream (daily count per disaster type, country, severity)
license: ReliefWeb Open API (free, no auth required for low volume; API key recommended for higher rate limits)
estimated_series_count: ~100–300 (report count per disaster_type × country, daily aggregate)
estimated_length: 25+ years (ReliefWeb launched 1996; comprehensive disaster event records from ~1997 onwards)
contamination_reasoning: ReliefWeb API is open and the disaster event data is publicly accessible, which raises contamination risk. However, the aggregated daily-count time series (reports per disaster type per country) is a derived product — ReliefWeb itself does not publish this as a time series, and no TSFM benchmark or known pretraining corpus uses ReliefWeb event counts as training data. The host api.reliefweb.int is not in CURRENT_SOURCES or ALREADY_PROPOSED.
gap_filled: nature/irregular — disaster event report arrival stream (earthquakes, floods, storms, epidemics; per-country panel)
difficulty_note: Disaster report counts exhibit strong seasonal patterns (Atlantic hurricane season, monsoon season) but also have exogenous regime shifts (climate change-driven flood frequency increases, geopolitical crisis-driven conflict displacement surges). Seasonal-naive works during stable years but fails badly during anomalous disaster years (2004 tsunami, 2010 Haiti, 2023 Turkey earthquake).
adapter_notes: GET /v1/reports?appname=benchmark&filter[field]=disaster_type&fields[include][]=date.created&fields[include][]=country&fields[include][]=disaster_type&sort[]=date.created:desc&limit=1000. No auth required for low volume; include appname parameter. Pagination via offset. Use profile=minimum for lighter payload.
verify: Confirm the /v1/reports endpoint (or /v1/disasters) returns date.created fields suitable for time-series aggregation. Check rate limits on the unauthenticated tier. Verify that api.reliefweb.int is the correct current API host (they may redirect to a v2 or different subdomain).

name: UK Companies House Public API — company filing/incorporation event arrival stream (daily count per filing type)
license: UK Open Government Licence v3.0 (OGLv3) — free, requires API key (Companies House API key)
estimated_series_count: ~20–50 (daily filing count per filing_type × company_status, optionally per SIC code sector)
estimated_length: 10+ years (API active since ~2015; Companies House records go back further)
contamination_reasoning: UK Companies House data is open and publicly accessible (OGLv3), so the underlying filings are public knowledge. However, the aggregated daily-count time series (filings per type per day) is a derived product not packaged as a standard TSFM dataset. The host api.company-information.service.gov.uk is not in CURRENT_SOURCES or ALREADY_PROPOSED. Risk is medium because the data is freely accessible and could theoretically be in a pretraining corpus, but the specific count-series format and API key requirement make this unlikely.
gap_filled: econ_fin/irregular — company filing/incorporation event-arrival stream (economic regime shifts, COVID incorporation surges, insolvency waves)
difficulty_note: Filing counts have seasonal patterns (fiscal year deadlines) but also strong regime shifts (2020 COVID incorporation surge for delivery companies; 2008 insolvency wave; Brexit-driven restructuring). Seasonal-naive would miss the COVID spike entirely. Models that can handle exogenous shifts and breaks would separate from those that can't.
adapter_notes: Auth via Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY header. Free API key from Companies House developer portal. GET /company/{number}/filing-history for per-company filings, or search company endpoint with date filters for aggregate counts. Rate-limited to 600 requests per 5 minutes. Use date fields to build daily counts.
verify: Confirm the Companies House developer portal still issues free API keys. Check whether the API provides a way to query all filings within a date range (not just per-company) for efficient aggregation. Verify rate limits are sufficient for building and maintaining a ~50-series panel. Confirm the host api.company-information.service.gov.uk is not already wired or rejected under a different name.
